ds: Use of businesses that naturally handle large cash volumes, such as restaurants, car washes, laundromats, vending, convenience stores and nail salons, to blend illicit cash with legitimate takings. Deposits are inflated to fit the business's apparent scale.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering Typologies: cash-intensive business guidance (general)
FinCEN, SAR Activity Review on cash-intensive businesses (general)
JMLSG Guidance Part II, sector guidance on cash-intensive customers (general)

cn.rt: Sole traders banking inflated cash takings via personal Everyday or savings accounts, mainly over the counter; merchant and business-only elements are out of scope.

rat: Restaurants, car washes, laundromats and similar cash-heavy businesses deposit inflated takings at branches and ATMs; card acquiring also relevant.

ind.n: Cash deposits exceed plausible business capacity
ind.cx: Declared turnover or deposits are higher than the premises size, staffing, opening hours or stock purchases would support.
ind.fp: New or fast-growing businesses can legitimately outperform peers.
ind.ds: Declared turnover or deposits are higher than the premises size, staffing, opening hours or stock purchases would support.

ind.n: Deposits unsupported by supplier or cost-of-sales activity
ind.cx: Cash takings are high but there are few payments to suppliers, rent, wages or tax authorities.
ind.fp: Cash-paid suppliers or off-account costs may exist.
ind.ds: Cash takings are high but there are few payments to suppliers, rent, wages or tax authorities.

ind.cx: Step-change in deposit values or frequency without explanation such as new outlets or season.
ind.fp: Expansion, promotion or events can explain growth.
ind.ds: Step-change in deposit values or frequency without explanation such as new outlets or season.

ind.n: Business type inconsistent with location or customer base
ind.cx: Cash business operating where demand appears limited, with few visible customers or irregular hours.
ind.fp: Online-only operations or early-stage businesses may appear quiet.
ind.ds: Cash business operating where demand appears limited, with few visible customers or irregular hours.

ind.n: Cash deposits mixed with unrelated third-party funds
ind.cx: Deposits include cheques, transfers or cash from persons unconnected to trading, or rotated across several business accounts.
ind.fp: Owners may inject funds legitimately as capital.
ind.ds: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
ind.cn: Payments from or to unrelated third parties

ind.n: Ownership or management opaque for cash business
ind.cx: Unclear beneficial owners, nominee directors or frequent ownership change in a cash business.
ind.fp: Family businesses may have informal arrangements.
ind.ds: Ownership or governance is opaque and no natural person who owns or controls the entity can be identified after reasonable effort.
ind.cn: Beneficial owner or controller cannot be identified

ind.n: Large cash withdrawals paired with deposits of equivalent value
ind.cx: Cash is repeatedly withdrawn and redeposited, or round-tripped with associated accounts.
ind.fp: Float management for tills may look similar.
ind.ds: Cash is repeatedly withdrawn and redeposited, or round-tripped with associated accounts.

ind.n: Multiple cash businesses controlled by same people
ind.cx: Common owners or addresses across several cash businesses with cross-funding.
ind.fp: Franchise or serial entrepreneurs are common.
ind.ds: Several apparently separate businesses or sub-accounts share owners, signatories, addresses, devices or bank accounts.

ctl.n: Cash deposit profiling and peer benchmarking
ctl.ds: Compares cash deposits and withdrawals with expected activity, sector and location peers and declared turnover, alerting on outliers. It helps find cash that is inconsistent with the stated business.
Reconciles cash, stock purchases, sales and exports with declared business activity to test whether deposits are plausible. It is used to identify unrecorded or injected cash.
Compares account flows with filed accounts, VAT or sales tax data and tax remittances, and links to VAT-fraud controls. It spots under-declared revenue and tax fraud proceeds.

Contacts the customer, or the relationship manager does so, to obtain and record an explanation of unusual transactions, relationships or recipients, and to test it against evidence. The answer informs whether activity is legitimate or should be escalated.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.
